conditions.name: Common Cold
conditions.description: A frequent viral infection of the nose and throat (upper respiratory tract). It is typically harmless, though it might not feel that way, and usually resolves within 7 to 10 days.
precautions: Get plenty of physical rest to help your immune system fight the virus.
Stay well hydrated by drinking warm water, herbal teas, or clear broths.
Gargle with warm salt water to relieve throat irritation and soreness.
Use saline nasal drops or steam inhalation to alleviate nasal congestion.
Wash hands regularly with soap to avoid transmitting the virus to family or colleagues.
next_steps: Monitor symptoms closely over the next 5 to 7 days.
Consult a general physician if fever exceeds 101.3°F (38.5°C) or symptoms persist beyond 10 days.
Consult a licensed pharmacist before taking over-the-counter decongestants or lozenges.

conditions.name: Flu (Influenza)
conditions.description: A contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses that infect the nose, throat, and sometimes the lungs. It is characterized by sudden onset of high fever and generalized aches.
precautions: Isolate at home during the febrile period to prevent community spread.
Consume ample fluids including warm soups, oral rehydration fluids, and water.
Avoid strenuous work or vigorous exercise until fever and body aches subside completely.
Disinfect high-touch household surfaces such as doorknobs and phones.
next_steps: Consult a doctor within the first 48 hours if antiviral medications might be advised.
Seek urgent medical evaluation if you experience persistent high fever or chest heaviness.
Schedule a clinical follow-up if your health improves initially but subsequently relapses.

conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.description: A neurological disorder characterized by recurrent, moderate-to-severe throbbing headaches, frequently unilateral (affecting one side), often triggered by stress, dietary factors, or sensory stimulation.
precautions: Rest in a quiet, dark, and comfortably cool environment during an episode.
Apply a cold pack or soothing compress to your forehead or the nape of your neck.
Maintain regular hydration and avoid skipping scheduled meals.
Avoid known dietary triggers such as aged cheeses, monosodium glutamate (MSG), or excessive caffeine.
next_steps: Maintain a headache diary recording onset time, duration, and potential environmental triggers.
Schedule an appointment with a neurologist or physician for dedicated headache management.
Seek emergency care if this is the sudden 'worst headache of your life' or accompanied by speech loss.

conditions.name: Tension Headache
conditions.description: The most common variety of headache, producing diffuse, mild to moderate aching pain often described as a tight band wrapped around the forehead, scalp, or neck.
precautions: Take periodic screen breaks (following the 20-20-20 rule) during computer use.
Perform gentle neck, shoulder, and upper back stretching exercises.
Apply a warm heating pad to tight shoulder or neck muscles to induce relaxation.
Practice progressive relaxation techniques or diaphragmatic breathing to reduce stress.
next_steps: Evaluate your desk ergonomic setup, chair support, and pillow firmness.
Consult a doctor if headaches recur more than two times weekly or disrupt daily activities.
Discuss safe, non-habit-forming pain management options with a healthcare provider.

conditions.name: Food Poisoning
conditions.description: An acute illness caused by consuming contaminated, spoiled, or toxic food or water. Microorganisms such as bacteria or toxins irritate the gastrointestinal tract, triggering acute distress.
precautions: Take frequent, small sips of Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) or electrolyte water.
Refrain from solid meals for the first few hours until the stomach settles.
Gradually introduce bland foods (such as rice, bananas, dry toast, boiled potatoes).
Strictly avoid dairy products, caffeine, spicy items, and fried meals for several days.
next_steps: Seek professional medical attention if vomiting prevents fluid retention for more than 24 hours.
Consult a doctor immediately if you notice blood in stool, high fever, or signs of intense dehydration.
Avoid taking over-the-counter anti-motility drugs without prior clinical instruction.

conditions.name: Gastroenteritis (Stomach Flu)
conditions.description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines typically caused by viral or bacterial infection, characterized by loose watery stools, abdominal cramping, and nausea.
precautions: Rehydrate continuously with electrolyte-balanced fluids and diluted broths.
Wash hands thoroughly with soap after using the bathroom and before handling food.
Disinfect shared bathrooms and living quarters to safeguard household members.
Rest adequately to assist bodily recovery.
next_steps: Monitor for indications of moderate to severe dehydration (dry tongue, reduced urination, lightheadedness).
Consult a medical doctor if diarrhea continues past 48 to 72 hours.
Seek clinical consultation for stool testing if bacterial causes are suspected.

conditions.name: Dehydration
conditions.description: A physiological condition resulting from excessive fluid loss without adequate replenishment, causing the body's cells and circulatory volume to operate below optimal capacity.
precautions: Immediately consume room-temperature water or oral electrolyte solutions in measured sips.
Move out of direct heat or sun into a shaded, air-conditioned, or well-ventilated room.
Avoid caffeinated soft drinks, energy drinks, and alcohol which exacerbate fluid depletion.
Lie down with feet slightly elevated if experiencing feelings of faintness or dizziness.
next_steps: Continue systematic rehydration over the next 4 to 6 hours.
Visit an urgent care center or clinic if you cannot tolerate oral liquids or feel disoriented.
Seek urgent emergency treatment if accompanied by rapid heart rate, confusion, or syncope (fainting).

conditions.name: Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever)
conditions.description: An allergic response of the nasal mucosa triggered by hypersensitivity to airborne allergens such as pollen, dust mites, pet dander, or mold spores.
precautions: Keep residential windows closed during peak pollen hours (early morning and windy days).
Use certified HEPA air purification filters inside sleeping areas.
Take a shower and change clothing after spending extended time outdoors.
Perform gentle saline nasal rinses to flush trapped allergens out of nasal cavities.
next_steps: Consult a general physician or allergist for diagnostic allergy confirmation.
Seek guidance from a doctor regarding suitable antihistamines, nasal corticosteroids, or decongestants.
Seek emergency care if symptoms ever evolve into wheezing, facial swelling, or breathing distress.
